evidence: Declared as 1 of 14 families but absent from all 1,260 family rows in price_panel.csv. 'Punch & mixed fruit' is ordered earlier and its regex contains `melon`, so it swallows every melon string; only a bare 'cantaloupe' can reach it, and 'cucumber' loses to 'Tea & botanical' on `mint`.
options: (a) delete the family; (b) move it above 'Punch & mixed fruit'; (c) keep it documented as dead

item: 'Mango Peach' resolves to Tropical, not Peach
evidence: 'Tropical' is ordered before 'Peach & stone fruit' and matches `mango`, so the literal `mango peach` alternative inside the Peach regex is unreachable dead code.
options: (a) accept Tropical and delete the dead alternative; (b) hoist a two-fruit rule above both
recommendation: (a). The dead alternative implies an intent the code does not honour, which is worse than either assignment.

evidence: 'Grape Slush' -> 'Sour & candy' (not Grape) because `slush` sits in the earlier rule. Same for 'Blue Razz', 'Cotton Candy'. This is a real choice: it groups by the SENSORY PROMISE (candy-sweet) rather than the fruit. It materially affects Alani Nu, whose slush line is a growth driver.
options: (a) keep format-first; (b) let fruit win and treat candy/slush as a separate flag column
recommendation: (b) for this study. 'Which flavor sells' is a fruit question; candy-format is a second, orthogonal attribute and collapsing the two loses the ability to ask either cleanly.

item: Cherry is Berry, not stone fruit
evidence: `cherry` sits inside the Berry regex. Botanically a stone fruit; commercially it behaves like a berry (Cherry Limeade, Cherry Slush). Deliberate in the source, per CLAUDE.md.
options: (a) keep in Berry; (b) move to Peach & stone fruit
recommendation: (a) keep. Commercial behaviour beats botany for a go-to-market study - but state it in the methods note, because a reader will notice.

item: Prime is in the brief but not in the PDI top 22
evidence: ~$1.8M T12M (~0.13% share) against Bang's $21.9M. PDI also carries 'PRIME ENERGY ...' and 'PRIME ... SPORTS DRINKS' descriptions under one brand string - two different products.
options: (a) drop Prime; (b) keep as Tier B case study; (c) keep and split energy vs hydration SKUs
recommendation: (b), and filter to 'PRIME ENERGY' descriptions only if it ever enters a sales ranking. Prime's hydration line is not an energy drink and must not be summed into one.

item: Ghost is normalised two different ways
evidence: segments: 'Ghost Energy' $35.96M + 'Ghost' $6.96M. brand_momentum: 'Ghost' $42.86M. The sum reconciles, so it is a normalisation difference and not a data difference.
options: (a) adopt the merged form in brand_alias; (b) keep split if the two are genuinely different lines
recommendation: (a) merged, unless Ghost sells a non-energy line in this panel - check before freezing.

item: The brand ranking has no recorded query
evidence: add_bq_panels.py points at `data/sql/*.sql`; pos-momentum.js points at `docs/bigquery-findings.md`. NEITHER EXISTS in this repo. So the category filter, date window and brand normalisation behind brand_momentum_real.csv are unverified.
options: (a) re-derive from pdi_daily_agg and commit the SQL; (b) cite the CSV as-is
recommendation: (a), before the committee sees a number from it. This is the weakest link in WS0: every brand share here inherits an unaudited WHERE clause.

item: Ranking is by revenue; the brief says volume
evidence: brand_momentum_real.csv carries dollars only. Red Bull's price per ounce is above the category average, so its 37.9% revenue share overstates its unit share.
options: (a) re-rank on SUM(QUANTITY); (b) keep revenue and relabel every axis 'revenue share'
recommendation: (a). WS2 ranks on velocity in UNITS per store-week anyway, so the universe should be selected on the same basis it will be measured on.
